name: Ceephax Acid Crew
editorial_article: Ceephax Acid Crew is the primary performance moniker of British electronic musician Andy Jenkinson, a figurehead of the UK's underground acid house and drill and bass scenes. The name itself is a pun on the now-defunct BBC Ceefax teletext service, reflecting the nostalgic, hardware-obsessed, and often humorous tone of his output. Jenkinson is highly regarded for his mastery of analog synthesis, frequently utilizing classic gear like the Roland TB-303, TR-808, and TR-909 to create high-energy, infectious music that bridges the gap between old-school acid house, rave culture, and more complex electronic structures. \n\nHis career, which gained significant traction in the late 1990s and early 2000s, is inextricably linked to the influential Rephlex Records label, co-founded by Aphex Twin. It was through this platform that Jenkinson developed his reputation as an essential live act, known for chaotic, hands-on, and blistering hardware performances that prioritize raw energy over rigid production polish. Over the decades, he has remained a prolific creator, constantly exploring the intersections of IDM, techno, and electro while retaining a distinct, playful aesthetic that sets him apart from more serious or austere electronic peers. His sustained relevance is punctuated by his ongoing association with modern collectives and labels like WéMè and Analogical Force, ensuring his status as a veteran stalwart of independent British electronic music. Throughout his discography, he remains a champion of the 'DIY' spirit, keeping the raw, unadulterated aesthetic of early acid house alive while pushing it into new, hyper-kinetic directions.

editorial_bio: Ceephax Acid Crew (Andy Jenkinson) is a prolific British electronic musician celebrated for his acid house, drill and bass, and IDM-infused hardware live performances. A long-term collaborator with the influential Rephlex Records, he is renowned for his mastery of the Roland TB-303 and his playful, energetic take on retro-futuristic rave aesthetics.
